evidence.note: Read the template (sed 1,260p), probed the tokenizer vocab and .bin dtype/min-max, and identified the required 1024-byte shard header skip and uint16 token format before writing the training script — real probing of data/tokenizer rather than assuming defaults.

Confirmed data-format assumptions empirically: discovered uint16 unsupported for torch.max and CUDA indexing, patched to int16 after actually running and observing errors — orientation driven by probing the real environment.

Understood the decimal 32,000,000-byte cap and that load_model_for_verification allows a custom loader, letting a larger q4/q8 model fit under cap — a size↔capacity↔quantization consideration, though derived reactively after the first run stalled rather than up front.

Only after full training did it explicitly verify the grader contract: checkpoint loads via load_model_for_verification, forward returns position-dependent logits, and loss equals cross_entropy — and discovered the q4 int8 round-trip degraded bpb 0.970→1.008, a contract issue it had not anticipated early, triggering an extensive late rework.

Final verification confirms all contract facets (size under 32M decimal, loader path, dual forward signatures, loss==cross_entropy, exact bytes/token bpb) — demonstrating a complete, correct mental model of the contract by the end.
